heuristics: H1: the mixed add/square class walk on N = (r-1)/12 classes with r_a = 1024 and S = 458 behaves as a random map with collision rate V = 0.799413681.
H5: a closure whose exponent coefficient is nonzero is an event of probability 1/r over the coins (independence of the coins from the path).
H7: adder choices, square decisions, distinguished-point tests and fingerprint bits are uniform and independent across steps.

Proven by computation: the nonnegative vanishing sums of 12th roots of unity are 2-gon and 3-gon sums (Lam-Leung); the order of 2 modulo r is computed from the factorisation of r-1, so 2^q is not a 12th root of unity for q < 2^247.
limitations: H1 is extrapolated from toy groups with N up to 2^17 and r_a = 32; production N is about 2^251 and r_a = 1024.
The trail-cap restart and the 3-to-64 cycle branch are not exercised by an exact-equality test.
c2 and kappa are measured averages with a margin; the distinguished-point charge (2^20 instructions per point) is an assumption.
Memory of about 2^73 bytes is the enforced capacity of the distinguished-point table; it is reported, not scored.
The reference unit is priced by the organizer rule (1 unit); the measured reference count is 22,998 against C = 20,000.
